one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-03 to 2026-11-01. AAOI's Q3 print is expected ~Nov 5 (StockAnalysis estimate; prior Q3 8-K 2.02 filings came 2025-11-06 and 2024-11-07; no date 8-K yet), so I put only ~5-10% on an in-window print or pre-announcement. In-window: hyperscaler Q3 results and 2027 capex commentary (late Oct) and Chinese module makers' Q3 reports (Innolight/Eoptolink/Accelink by Oct 31), which move optical names as a group in an unknown direction; ongoing sales under the $600M ATM are a mild negative drift. No valuation view belongs in a 1-month forecast, so I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on $115.59 with a ~1.2% negative tilt for ATM supply and a monthly sigma of 0.38 (139% annual / ~3.6), giving P(>=115.59)=0.487.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E ($4.20 haircut NTM-at-Oct-2027 EPS x 21x = $88, weight 0.45), EV/EBITDA ($630M x 14x + $0.2B net cash over 98M shares = $92, weight 0.30) and the probability-weighted scenario value ($104, weight 0.25). Multiples are the 10-peer CY27 medians (P/E ~27x, EV/EBITDA proxy ~18x) rolled one year forward for peer earnings growth, with no added premium or discount.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027-basis P/E 15.75x (Innolight) to 47.8x (Accelink). Sorted: Innolight 15.75, JBL ~16.5, Eoptolink 18.65, FN ~22.3, CLS 24.9, COHR ~29, LITE ~40, CIG 41.2, HGTECH 41.5, Accelink 47.8; median ~27x. Basis: CLS, Innolight and Eoptolink are CY27 as published (Innolight and Eoptolink checked against ~RMB61B and ~RMB29-30B CY27 NI estimates); Accelink is computed from CY27 consensus EPS ¥3.45 (StockAnalysis's own 65.4x 'forward PE' is not CY27, which confirms the mixed basis); FN, COHR and LITE are June-FY27 EPS rolled forward half a year at their FY27 growth (approximate); JBL is Aug-FY27 rolled forward (approximate); CIG and HGTECH use StockAnalysis forward P/E with the basis assumed to be CY27, unverified. Subsets: US/global-listed (JBL, FN, CLS, COHR, LITE) median ~24.9x; Chinese module makers median ~41x. Forward EV/EBITDA figures are all constructed proxies (trailing EV/EBITDA x forward P/E / trailing P/E; LITE as P/E/1.25 because it has a GAAP loss; JBL from forward operating growth because its trailing GAAP P/E is depressed), range ~11-52x, median ~18.3x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: AAOI trades today at ~25.1x the verified CY27 consensus ($115.59 / $4.60), slightly below the ~27x 10-peer median and in line with the ~25x US/global-listed subset. I value AAOI at Oct-2027 on NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) EPS at 21x and EBITDA at 14x. Those are the peer medians rolled forward one year for ~25-40% peer earnings growth, inside the 15.8-47.8x and ~11-52x ranges.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium or discount to the rolled-forward peer median is applied. I considered a discount for AAOI's ~30% GM, negative FCF and 92% top-3 concentration, but the peer set does not show that low margins are persistently penalised: the low-GM Chinese module makers (Accelink 22%, CIG 26%, HGTECH 20%) trade at the top of the range and the 45-48% GM leaders (Innolight, Eoptolink) at the bottom, because the market prices the stage of the earnings inflection rather than the margin level. AAOI's specific risks (dilution, unproven operating profit, concentration) are put into the share count (~98M), a 10% EPS haircut and a 30% bear weight rather than into the multiple, to avoid counting them twice. I also see no evidence for a persistent premium: the US-supply argument is not yet visible in AAOI's pricing or margins. This differs from the supervisor's ~21x CY27 median, which used six peers; with the brief's 10 to 12 peers the CY27 median is ~27x (~25x for the US/global-listed subset). In my valuation the difference mostly disappears, because I apply ~21x to NTM-at-horizon (CY28-weighted) EPS, not to CY27.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$58 (EV ~$5.5B on ~98M shares, ~12.6x the verified $4.60 FY27 consensus and below the lowest peer CY27 multiple of 15.75x) the market would be pricing NTM EPS near $2.5, i.e. a failed or badly delayed 1.6T ramp, a cut at one of the three customers that make up 92% of revenue, or GM stuck below 30% with the 2026 capex unrecovered. That sits below the 2026 drawdown lows ($76 in July, ~$94 in September), so ordinary volatility is unlikely to reach it without a fundamental break.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's evidence-backed findings change my numbers in four places. (1) The Q2 'non-GAAP profit' was a $14.3M tax add-back with Adj. EBITDA of -$0.5M, so my round-1 EBITDA bridge (26% margin in FY27, $850M in FY28) was unsupported. I rebuilt it from today's ~0% margin: $3.0B NTM-at-horizon revenue x 31% GM less ~$380-390M opex gives ~$700M EBITDA and ~$4.68 EPS before a 10% execution haircut. (2) Peer multiples: my Chinese peer figures were wrong (Innolight 15.75x and Eoptolink 18.65x, both checked as CY27), and the round-1 median of 36.7x mixed fiscal years and included fabless semis. I rebuilt a 10-peer set of module makers and optical/AI hardware manufacturers on a CY27 basis: median ~27x, range 15.8-47.8x. The supervisor's 21x came from six peers; I keep my wider set because the brief asks for 10-12 and the low-margin Chinese module makers are genuine comparables. I apply ~21x to NTM-at-horizon EPS, which is the median rolled forward a year, so my valuation multiple lands close to the supervisor's anyway. (3) Net cash ~$0.2B, ~98M diluted shares and capacity of 650k units/month at YE26 rising to 930k by end-27 are confirmed. (4) I drop the unsourced 'Amazon $220B capex' claim. Fair value falls from $120 to $93 (P/E $88, EV/EBITDA $92, scenario value $104). The industry evidence still supports demand: LightCounting has Ethernet transceivers +65% in 2026 with supply short, Coherent datacom is +59%, Lumentum +109%, and Innolight's orders run into 2027. Price cuts and the margin gap to the Chinese leaders cap AAOI's economics. The ladder is a three-scenario lognormal mixture: bear $50 (30%, sigma 0.55), base $102 (45%, sigma 0.38), bull $180 (25%, sigma 0.45). It has mean ~$117, close to spot, and a median of ~$100 because of the very high volatility (139% realized). P(>=$116)=0.39. The far-left tail is fattened to P(>=$29)=0.95, reflecting AAOI's -90% drawdown history and tangible book of ~$20/share. Research in this round was 2 web searches plus ~16 StockAnalysis page fetches; Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage were not used.
